stem: See fig 2.11. In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\angle A = 30^\circ\), AC = 14, then find AB and BC.
solution:
In \(\triangle ABC\),
\(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\angle A = 30^\circ\), \(\therefore\) \(\angle C = 60^\circ\)

By \(30^\circ - 60^\circ - 90^\circ\) theorem,

\(BC = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AC\)

\(BC = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 14\)

\(BC = 7\)

\(AB = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times AC\)

\(AB = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 14\)

\(AB = 7\sqrt{3}\)

stem: See fig 2.12, In \(\triangle ABC\), seg AD \(\perp\) seg BC, \(\angle C = 45^\circ\), BD = 5 and AC = \(8\sqrt{2}\) then find AD and BC.
solution:
In \(\triangle ADC\)

\(\angle ADC = 90^\circ\), \(\angle C = 45^\circ\), \(\therefore\) \(\angle DAC = 45^\circ\)

\(AD = DC = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times 8\sqrt{2}\) ... by \(45^\circ - 45^\circ - 90^\circ\) theorem

\(DC = 8\)   \(\therefore\) \(AD = 8\)

\(BC = BD + DC\)

\(\ \ \ \ = 5 + 8\)

\(BC = 13\)

stem: In fig 2.13, \(\angle PQR = 90^\circ\), seg QN \(\perp\) seg PR, PN = 9, NR = 16. Find QN.
solution:
In \(\triangle PQR\), seg QN \(\perp\) seg PR

\(NQ^2 = PN \times NR\) ... theorem of geometric mean

\(\therefore NQ = \sqrt{PN \times NR}\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ = \sqrt{9 \times 16}\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 3 \times 4\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 12\)

stem:
See figure 2.14. In \(\triangle PQR\), \(\angle PQR = 90^\circ\), seg QS \(\perp\) seg PR then find \(x\), \(y\), \(z\).

(From fig. 2.14: S lies on seg PR, PS = 10, SR = 8, QS = \(x\), QR = \(y\), PQ = \(z\).)
solution:
In \(\triangle PQR\), \(\angle PQR = 90^\circ\), seg QS \(\perp\) seg PR

\(QS = \sqrt{PS \times SR}\) .......... (theorem of geometric mean)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ = \sqrt{10 \times 8}\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ = \sqrt{5 \times 2 \times 8}\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ = \sqrt{5 \times 16}\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ = 4\sqrt{5}\)

\(\therefore x = 4\sqrt{5}\)

In \(\triangle QSR\), by Pythagoras theorem

\(QR^2 = QS^2 + SR^2\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = \left(4\sqrt{5}\right)^2 + 8^2\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 16 \times 5 + 64\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 80 + 64\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 144\)

\(\therefore QR = 12\)

In \(\triangle PSQ\), by Pythagoras theorem

\(PQ^2 = QS^2 + PS^2\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = \left(4\sqrt{5}\right)^2 + 10^2\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 16 \times 5 + 100\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 80 + 100\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 180\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 36 \times 5\)

\(\therefore PQ = 6\sqrt{5}\)

Hence \(x = 4\sqrt{5}\), \(y = 12\), \(z = 6\sqrt{5}\)

stem: In the right angled triangle, sides making right angle are 9 cm and 12 cm. Find the length of the hypotenuse.
solution:
In \(\triangle PQR\), \(\angle Q = 90^\circ\)

\(PR^2 = PQ^2 + QR^2\) (Pythagoras theorem)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 9^2 + 12^2\)

\(\ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 81 + 144\)

\(PR^2 = 225\)

\(PR = 15\)

Hypotenuse = 15 cm

stem: In \(\triangle LMN\), \(l = 5\), \(m = 13\), \(n = 12\). State whether \(\triangle LMN\) is a right angled triangle or not.
solution:
\(l = 5\), \(m = 13\), \(n = 12\)

\(l^2 = 25\), \(m^2 = 169\), \(n^2 = 144\)

\(\therefore m^2 = l^2 + n^2\)

\(\therefore\) by converse of Pythagoras theorem \(\triangle LMN\) is a right angled triangle.

stem: See fig 2.16. In \(\triangle ABC\), seg AD \(\perp\) seg BC. Prove that: \(AB^2 + CD^2 = BD^2 + AC^2\)
solution:
According to Pythagoras theorem, in \(\triangle ADC\)

\(AC^2 = AD^2 + CD^2\)

\(\therefore AD^2 = AC^2 - CD^2\) ... (I)

In \(\triangle ADB\)

\(AB^2 = AD^2 + BD^2\)

\(\therefore AD^2 = AB^2 - BD^2\) ... (II)

\(\therefore AB^2 - BD^2 = AC^2 - CD^2\) .......... from I and II

\(\therefore AB^2 + CD^2 = AC^2 + BD^2\)
